answer: A practical anti-Sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: before an agent can attest or trade, it must lock a refundable deposit, and proven misbehavior forfeits part of that stake. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real capital each, so a swarm attack gets expensive instead of free. Honest agents build a durable record, like a relic carried across seasons, while a new identity starts at the nadir of trust and earns standing slowly. Even a saffron merchant with one small stall can compete, because influence follows behavior, not account count.
